title: The morning-after cover
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover: the beach the morning after the run — lantern stubs in the sand, bucket rings, a hundred footprints and one set of paw prints going the other way. The owner says it looks like a party. Wood says it was.

panels.composition: The cover: the beach at dawn, lantern stubs, rings in the sand where buckets sat, footprints everywhere, and one line of paw prints going the wrong way.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing a beach at dawn with lantern stubs, bucket rings and many footprints in the sand crossed by one line of paw prints, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner with it. WOOD. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet while a young man and a small dog wait, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The paw prints on the cover. Going the wrong way. The owner's thumb on them.

image.prompt: close on a booklet cover with a line of small paw prints under a woman's thumb, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The cover facing the room. Outside the window, the real beach is two blocks off and the tide has taken the prints already. The cover has them.

image.prompt: a wire rack in a laundromat holding a booklet, a gray beach visible far down the street through the window, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Third year.' The tide has the prints; the cover keeps them.
